title: Integral concentration for torus-equivariant coherent classes
statement:
For an affine finite-type group scheme $G$ over a field $F$ [def-weil-field, def-sc-group-scheme] acting on an $F$-scheme $Y$ [def-pc-scheme], a $G$-linearized coherent module means a coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-module [pqf-def-coherent] with an isomorphism $a^*\mathcal M\simeq\operatorname{pr}_2^*\mathcal M$ on $G\times_FY$, satisfying the identity and cocycle identities; its geometric fibre action is from $y$ to $gy$. Let $G_0^G(Y)$ be the abelian group on isomorphism classes of these modules, with relations $[\mathcal M]=[\mathcal M']+[\mathcal M'']$ for every equivariant short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal M'\to\mathcal M\to\mathcal M''\to0$. Let $R(G)$ be the analogous group of finite-dimensional rational $G$-modules, with multiplication induced by tensor product. Rational means a counital coassociative coaction $V\to V\otimes_FF[G]$. Tensoring a sheaf with the trivial vector bundle associated to such a module makes $G_0^G(Y)$ an $R(G)$-module. Suppose $F$ is algebraically closed [def-weil-algebraic-closure], $G=T\simeq\mathbf G_m^r$ is a split torus, and $Y$ is a smooth projective $F$-scheme [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-pc-morphism-conventions] with an algebraic $T$-action. Here $\mathbf G_m(A)=A^\times$. Set $X=\operatorname{Hom}(T,\mathbf G_m)$ and $R=\mathbf Z[X]$ with $e^\eta e^\xi=e^{\eta+\xi}$. The $R$-module structure on $G_0^T(Y)$ twists linearizations by the one-dimensional representations of characters $\eta$. Let $i:Y^T\hookrightarrow Y$ be the closed subscheme representing the functor of points fixed after every algebra extension; it is assumed to exist. Let $\Sigma$ be the multiplicative subset of $R$ generated by $1-e^\eta$ for all $\eta\ne0$. Then ordinary closed pushforward induces an isomorphism of localized $R$-modules
$$i_*:G_0^T(Y^T)\otimes_R R_\Sigma\ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\ G_0^T(Y)\otimes_R R_\Sigma.$$
The assertion uses integer Grothendieck groups in every characteristic, and includes $Y^T=\varnothing$ and $r=0$. No choice of an element of $T(F)$ with dense cyclic subgroup is required.

source.place: Section 22d, proof of Theorem 22.50, p.480: agent-supplied concentration prerequisite, not the numerical fixed-point formula itself. WANTED: Thomason, Une formule de Lefschetz en K-theorie equivariante algebrique, Duke Math. J. 53 (1986), concentration theorem; not present locally. No proof of concentration is claimed to occur in Milne.

proof.text: By [lem-pc-projective-proper] the structure morphism of $Y$ is proper, hence separated and of finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. The fixed closed subscheme $W=Y^T$ is invariant: every $T$-action morphism on its points is the identity by the representing fixed functor. Its open complement $U$ is invariant too. Apply [lem-sfb-equivariant-coherent-localization-sequence] to this closed/open pair, obtaining $\ker(j^*)=\operatorname{im}(i_*)$. The character map $R\to R(T)$ sends $e^\eta$ to the one-dimensional coaction $v\mapsto v\otimes\eta$. Tensoring two such coactions multiplies their characters, so this is a ring map and the cited $R(T)$-linearity makes $i_*$ and $j^*$ $R$-linear for precisely the twists stipulated in the item.

source.place: Agent proof of the concentration prerequisite for Milne, Theorem 22.50, printed p.480: localization on the nonfixed complement followed by regular self-intersection. Thomason (1986) is WANTED; this is not a proof attributed to Milne.

proof.text: Take any class $b/s$ in $G_0^T(Y)\otimes_RR_\Sigma$, using the fraction description of module localization. Apply [lem-sfb-torus-nonfixed-complement-annihilation] to $j^*b$. It gives $t\in\Sigma$ with $j^*(tb)=t\,j^*b=0$. Exactness from step 1 supplies $a\in G_0^T(W)$ with $i_*a=tb$. Therefore $i_*(a/(ts))=tb/(ts)=b/s$. This proves surjectivity, including $W=\varnothing$, when the source is zero. The element argument uses only the definition of localization; no rationalization, tensor-exactness hypothesis, or element of $T(F)$ with a dense cyclic subgroup occurs.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-torus-fixed-euler-unit] to the given smooth projective $Y$ and its represented fixed closed subscheme $W$. It supplies regularity of $i$ near $W$ with bounded regular-sequence lengths and says that the alternating conormal exterior tensor operator $L=\lambda_{-1}(N^\vee)$ is an automorphism of $G_0^T(W)\otimes_RR_\Sigma$. These are the geometric hypotheses and the invertibility needed for self-intersection; no affine smoothness theorem is applied to a projective scheme without an invariant affine cover.

source.place: Agent proof of the concentration prerequisite for Milne, Theorem 22.50, printed p.480: localization on the nonfixed complement followed by regular self-intersection. Thomason (1986) is WANTED; this is not a proof attributed to Milne.

proof.text: The hypotheses of [lem-sfb-equivariant-regular-self-intersection] now hold: $Y$ is separated of finite type by step 1, $i$ is an equivariant closed immersion, and its local regular sequences have bounded lengths by step 3. Its $R(T)$-linear map $i^!$ is $R$-linear along the character map of step 1, so it extends to the localization. The identity $i^!i_*=\lambda_{-1}(N^\vee)$ extends there as well. If $i_*\beta=0$, apply $i^!$ to get $L\beta=0$, then the inverse of $L$ from step 3 gives $\beta=0$. Thus $i_*$ is injective. Together with step 2 it is the asserted isomorphism of localized $R$-modules.

source.place: Agent proof of the concentration prerequisite for Milne, Theorem 22.50, printed p.480: localization on the nonfixed complement followed by regular self-intersection. Thomason (1986) is WANTED; this is not a proof attributed to Milne.

proof.text: For $r=0$, the action is that of the trivial group scheme, the representing fixed functor is all of $Y$, and $i$ is the identity; $X=0$ and $\Sigma=\{1\}$. The argument gives the identity on the unlocalized group. If $Y$ or $W$ is empty, a coherent module on the empty scheme is zero, and the same calculations apply to its zero Grothendieck group. All relations, annihilators and exterior-power identities used above are integral, so no characteristic-dependent division has entered.
